messages:
arjun: Brain-dump from the auth sync: we should standardize on a short-signed credential (v1) delivered as `X-RW-CLAIM` header. Not full JWTs — compact, fixed fields to minimize parsing cost. Fields: v, kid, sub, org, proj, orig_key, exp, auth_path.

marta: why not JWT? parsers + libraries already exist.

arjun: JWTs are flexible but heavy. We want single-pass parse + HMAC verification as the default for speed. Offer JWT-compat mode for partners who need more claims.

kevin: signing algs? HMAC exposes symmetric key management pain if we have many regions.

arjun: HMAC (HS256) for region-local signing keys stored in regional KMS for fastest verification. Global HSM (RS256) for cross-region federation and long-lived partner assertions. Proxy verifies HS by reading region KMS-derived key; if kid indicates RS, proxy fetches public key cache.

lena: ok but we need a clear key rotation story. If we rotate a signing key, how do we avoid invalidating all minted claims mid-flight?

arjun: include `kid` in claim and rotate with overlap windows: new key + old key accepted for N minutes. Also mint short `exp` (30-120s) for proxy-created claims. Long-lived operator keys get `orig_key` but we still mint intermediate claims.

marta: migration: clients that pass raw API keys - do we require them to change?

arjun: phased. 1) Proxy accepts `Authorization: Bearer <legacy>` OR `X-RW-CLAIM`. 2) On legacy, proxy can locally validate simple allowlist or do offline authn lookup and then mint a v1 claim. 3) After opt-in window we deprecate raw acceptance for write endpoints; read-only endpoints keep legacy for longer. 4) SDK will auto-exchange.

kevin: probe: some high-throughput customers will be sensitive to any extra proxy CPU for HMAC. Can we push authorizer decisions into the proxy (allow/deny) for hot paths?

arjun: yes — design has two enforcement tiers. Hot-path: proxy evaluates allowlist + scope-prefix checks using a tiny policy DSL embedded in proxy (cacheable). Cold-path: full authz call to central service when policy is complex. This reduces roundtrips for common cases.

lena: telemetry: we must preserve billing keys and orig_key in logs for invoices. Also tag requests with `auth_path` = {proxy_mint, client_claim, federated}.

arjun: yep — `orig_key` is mandatory in claims. Proxy also emits `auth_resolution_ms` and `auth_cache_hit` metrics.

marta: shadow testing strategy?

arjun: proxy runs both: evaluate new claim-based enforcement and the current legacy check and emit metric when results diverge. Also run sampling of full-audit traces (w/ orig_key) to catch failures.

sam-bot: ops-bot: scheduled job created to run divergence report daily at 02:00Z -> #eng-security :gear:

kevin: revocation model? blackout needs to be fast.

arjun: two mechanisms: 1) immediate: revoke key -> publish revocation event to region pubsub; proxies invalidate cache and drop further requests. 2) expirations: claims are short TTL so leaked minted claims are low blast. For operator tokens we enforce rotation windows and provide an emergency revocation that also toggles `accept_legacy=false` in proxy config.

lena: how to handle background jobs that cannot rotate quickly? They rely on operator tokens.

arjun: mark those as `key_type: operator` in claim. Proxies allow a slightly longer proxy-minted TTL for operator-authenticated flows but they still honor revocations. Recommend migrating infra to mTLS or workload identities in the mid-term.

kevin: metrics to collect before we flip enforcement?

arjun: per-route auth_cache_hit, auth_service_latency, auth_decision_divergence_rate, proxy_mint_rate, revocation_lag. We'll define SLOs for target p95 auth latency.

marta: SDK UX: automatic background exchange + fallback on network error?

arjun: SDK will attempt to exchange legacy key for claim at startup and refresh before expiry. If exchange fails, SDK retries with exponential backoff and continues to send legacy header until enforcement. Provide opt-in env var to force exchange.

lena: compliance: signed claims must include audit metadata and be verifiable by internal auditors. We should keep signature verification logs for 90 days.

arjun: noted. KMS audit + write-only signature logs will be stored in long-term logging.

kevin: last ask: include a clear sequence diagram and the tiny policy DSL spec in the RFC. Also perf microbenchmarks for parsing/verify cost at 1k rps.

arjun: will include sequence diagram, DSL doc, and bench numbers. I'll open RFC-116: "compact-claims-proxy-minting" and attach a migration timeline + opt-out gates. Target review by end of week.

marta: 👍 thanks, that captures it.
